requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from structural
hashes. The remaining source structure and text participate in hashing.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only and requested no implementation source. The tests adequately cover the TypeScript fingerprint obligations.

**Obligations derived from the subject**
1. Structural hashes are SHA-256 digests over the structural encoding. Text is hashed as whitespace-separated words, so the whitespace itself is never hashed and `ab cd` differs from `abcd`. This is defined under `requirements.references.structural_hash`, which the subject only cites.
2. The scheme identifies the TypeScript rules and their version. This is defined under `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`, which the subject only cites.
3. Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from the hash.
4. The remaining structure and text participate in the hash.

**Test mapping**
- **Comment exclusion (`.ts`).** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a TypeScript case.
  - The source has a `//` line comment and an inline `/* */` block comment in `function f`.
  - Changing the comment text leaves the hash equal.
  - Removing the comments entirely also leaves the hash equal.
  - Changing the non-comment literal (`1` to `2`) changes the hash. That covers obligation 4 and shows the exclusion isn't achieved by ignoring everything.
- **Doc comments and word rule (`.ts`, `.tsx`).** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has `.ts` and `.tsx` cases.
  - A `/** docs */` comment is changed or removed with no hash change. That covers documentation comments.
  - The string `"two words"` becomes `"two   words"` with no hash change. That covers whitespace not being hashed.
  - `"twowords"` produces a different hash. That covers the word-boundary rule.
- **Digest shape.** The same test asserts that each saved fingerprint value is 64 hex characters. It doesn't compare against a known SHA-256 value. The digest algorithm is defined by the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash`, so a check of the digest's shape is proportionate here.
- **Scheme.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts that `languages::TypeScript` reports `typescript-structural-v1` and `languages::Tsx` reports `tsx-structural-v1`. It also asserts that loaded `OutlineContent` retains the same scheme. The scheme definition belongs to the cited requirement, so I did not reassess it.

**Gaps**
I found no plausible requirement-violating TypeScript behavior that these tests would accept. All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject, so there is no marking gap.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments, including documentation comments, are excluded from structural
hashes. The remaining source structure and text participate in hashing.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
